title: Analyzing muscle structure and function throughout the larval instars in live Drosophila
protocol: Isolate 1st instar larvae of your desired genotypes from your vial/plate.
Clean larvae gently by immersing and swishing them in a watch glass containing ddH2O.
Transfer clean larvae to a fresh apple juice plate.
Set up imaging platform as shown (Figure 3A).
Place a fresh 10 cm wide apple juice agar plate below the imaging platform.
Place a ruler or measuring tape alongside the agar plate.
Acquire an image of the agar plate with ruler beside it.
Place larva from the first well of genotype of interest at the center of apple juice agar plate.
Start recording larval movement using a smartphone or camera for 45 s.
Choose a time period for tracking larval movement, e.g., 30, 45, or 60 seconds.
Allow larvae 2 seconds to acclimatize before recording their movement.
Record larval movement until 45 seconds is over or when the larva reaches the edge of the plate, whichever comes first.
Remove larva from plate using paintbrush and transfer back to well 1.
Transfer larva from well 2 to the plate and repeat tracking steps.
Track a maximum of 8 larvae on a single plate.
Change apple juice plate before tracking larvae from the next genotype.
Place plates with larvae back at 25°C after recording movements.
Isolate 2nd instar larvae after 24 hours and repeat all previous steps.
Repeat the process every 24 hours until larvae reach late 3rd instar stage.
Track larvae during the light cycle of the larva.
Dissect larvae individually once they reach late 3rd instar stage.
Fix dissected larvae as per Azevedo et al. (2016) protocol.
Stain fixed larvae according to the described method in Azevedo et al. (2016).
Mount stained larvae for examination of muscle structure.
Count the number of muscles with structural defects in each larva.
Score the severity of muscle structure defects in abdominal hemisegments A2-A7.
Divide affected muscles into different classes based on defect severity.
Plot percentages of defective muscles as graphs.
Calculate statistical significance using two-way ANOVA for defect analysis.
Repeat experiment with a new group of larvae for validation.
Clean 1st instar larvae by immersing them in ddH2O.
Transfer cleaned larvae to the lid of a 6-well plate containing Kwan Loong Medicated Oil.
Ensure that the larva does not dry out on the lid.
Add droplets of water to the larva using a paintbrush to prevent drying out.
Incubate larva in the chamber until it is anesthetized, i.e., stops moving when disturbed with a paintbrush.
Transfer anesthetized larvae to a microscope slide containing 50% glycerol and mount with a cover slip.
Record orientation of mounted larva (e.g., dorsal side up or down, head and mouth left or right).
Identify the hemisegments of the larval musculature to be imaged.
Image hemisegment(s) and record hemisegment numbers.
Carefully remove coverslip from larva after imaging.
Remove larva and wash gently with 1× PBS, then with ddH2O.
Transfer larva to clean apple juice plate until it awakens.
Once larva begins moving, transfer larva to the first well of larval collection plate.
Isolate second larva and repeat steps for anesthetizing, imaging, and transferring larvae until all desired genotypes have been imaged.
Move larval collection plate at 25°C in light-dark incubator after 24 h.
Isolate 2nd instar larvae and repeat the process every 24 hours until larvae reach late 3rd instar stage.
Set up laying pots of appropriate genotype containing fluorescent reporter(s) (e.g., Zasp-GFP) at 25°C.
Label and change apple juice plates on laying pots within 20 h, keeping the old ones for embryo and larva collection.
Isolate 1st instar larvae and distribute them into 3 different vials and an apple juice plate.
Pour enough water to cover embryos on the plate and remove dead flies using a paintbrush.
Gently disturb the embryos on the plate using a paintbrush and then transfer them to a collection basket.
Place the collection baskets in a plate with 50% bleach and dechorionate embryos for 4 min at room temperature.
Rinse the embryos in the collection basket with distilled water repeatedly to remove any traces of bleach.
Dip collection baskets with embryos into a water bath at 65°C for 1–2 s, ensuring that embryos are submerged in water.
Pick up larvae by the tail or head using forceps and submerge into a water bath at 65°C for 1–2 s.
Transfer embryos from the collection basket to a microscope slide using a paintbrush and then spread on the slide.
Mount embryos in either halocarbon oil or 50% glycerol, and cover with a coverslip.
Transfer larvae onto a microscope slide containing halocarbon oil or 50% glycerol.
Orient larvae such that their dorsal sides (containing trachea) are either parallel or perpendicular to the long axis of the slide.
Cover larvae with a cover slip.
Image the embryos or larvae immediately using a microscope.
Open image of muscle in Fiji.
Using Line tool draw a line from one end of the muscle to other.
Open an image of muscle in Fiji.
Draw a line from one Z-disc to the next using a line tool for measuring sarcomere width or number.
Register each measurement by selecting Analyze> Measure.
Repeat drawing and measuring lines between each successive pair of Z-discs throughout the length of the muscle.
Copy all measurement values into an Excel sheet.
Calculate average sarcomere size by averaging measurements from a single muscle.
Open the image of muscle in Fiji software.
Open the Cell Counter plugin by selecting Plugins > Cell Counter.
Select initialize option followed by Type 1 option in the pop-up window.
Click all Z lines within the muscle using the Cell Counter plugin.
Once all Z lines are counted, note the number next to the Type 1 option indicating sarcomere number.
Select Type 2 option and repeat counting for another muscle image.
Copy all measurement values into an Excel sheet.
Calculate average sarcomere number by averaging counts from different muscles.
Calculate sarcomere numbers from at least 10 different muscles.
Obtain data from 5 different larvae for each genotype.
Compare statistical significance of sarcomere numbers between genotypes using Student's t-test.
Determine statistical significance across different stages using multiple t-tests.
